page: Microsoft Azure E48d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 1933 GB of bundled local SSD space. There are no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in the middle tier of general enterprise compute. Multi-threaded performance shows solid capacity, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 11,270.0, a PassMark CPU score of 38,601.34, and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 44,668.06. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by an uncached read bandwidth of 165.21 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 83.52 GB/sec. Operational throughput benchmarks yield 40.15 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a PassMark database score of 16,136.08.

The primary performance tradeoff centers on per-core efficiency versus aggregate density. Single-threaded benchmarks fall into lower percentiles, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1,411.38 and single-threaded gzip compression registering at 23.78 GB/sec. Similarly, large language model text generation generates lower throughput without dedicated accelerators, producing 7.03 tokens per second on a 7B model. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of memory and high-capacity local scratch storage rather than burst single-thread execution.

The configuration is suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads that require high RAM capacity and local low-latency cache. Typical deployment targets include relational database servers, enterprise in-memory caching systems, distributed ETL jobs, and multi-threaded analytical processing.
